title: Wind-driven resuspension and turbidity recovery in a shallow eutrophic lake

headings.text: Wind-driven resuspension and turbidity recovery in a shallow eutrophic lake

key_sentences: We measured turbidity and wind speed at three stations in Lake Orrin, a shallow eutrophic lake with a mean depth of 2.1 m, during the autumn of 2025.
Turbidity rose within two hours of wind speeds exceeding 6 m/s and returned to baseline after a median of 31 hours.
A simple first-order decay model explained 78% of the variance in recovery times.
Shallow lakes are prone to sediment resuspension because wind-generated waves can reach the bed over most of their area.
Turbidity was recorded every 10 minutes with optical sensors, and wind speed was measured 4 m above the water surface.
Eleven resuspension events were identified between September and November.
Recovery was faster at the deeper stations, where less material was resuspended in the first place.
